Run all of these commands in your terminal, from inside your project folder.
You learnt uv in DSCI 521: for the full explanations, see the
[DSCI 521 notes on virtual environments with uv](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/virtual-environments-uv.html).

---

## The files in a uv project

| File | What it holds | Push to GitHub? |
|------|---------------|:---:|
| `pyproject.toml` | The packages **you asked for** (your shopping list) | ✅ |
| `uv.lock` | Every package **you got**, with exact versions and hashes, for every operating system (the receipt). Written by uv, never edit it by hand | ✅ |
| `.python-version` | The Python version for this project, e.g. `3.14` | ✅ |
| `.venv/` | The installed packages for **your** computer. Rebuilt with `uv sync` | ❌ |

## Start a new project

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Create a project (only makes `pyproject.toml`) | `uv init --bare` |
| Choose the Python version (makes `.python-version`) | `uv python pin 3.14` |
| Add a package (updates `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, builds `.venv/`) | `uv add pandas` |
| Add a specific version | `uv add "pandas==3.1.1"` |
| Add a package only needed for development, like testing | `uv add --dev pytest` |
| Remove a package | `uv remove pandas` |

### Make `uv add` write exact versions

By default `uv add pandas` writes `"pandas>=3.1.1"` (this version or newer) into `pyproject.toml`.
For a data analysis project, add these lines to `pyproject.toml`
so every `uv add` from now on writes an exact version (`"pandas==3.1.1"`):

```toml
[tool.uv]
add-bounds = "exact"
```

The setting only changes packages you add after it.

## Work on a project someone else made

```bash
git clone <URL>
cd <project folder>

# build .venv/ from uv.lock, exactly as on your teammate's computer
uv sync
```

## Run things in the environment

You do not need to activate the environment: put `uv run` in front of the command.

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Run a Python script | `uv run python script.py` |
| Run a one-line Python check | `uv run python -c "import pandas; print(pandas.__version__)"` |
| Render a Quarto report | `uv run quarto render report.qmd` |
| Run the tests | `uv run pytest` |

## Inspect and update

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Show which package pulls in which | `uv tree` |
| List what is installed in `.venv/` | `uv pip list` |
| Upgrade one package in `uv.lock`, then install it | `uv lock --upgrade-package pandas`, then `uv sync` |
| Check that `uv.lock` matches `pyproject.toml` (fails if not) | `uv lock --check` |
| Delete the environment and rebuild it | `rm -rf .venv`, then `uv sync` |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Add packages with `uv add`, not `uv pip install`
`uv pip install` does not write the package into `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`,
and the next `uv sync` removes it again.
:::

## Commands we ran in class (lecture 2)

```bash
# 1. make a new folder for the project and move into it
cd ~/Desktop/github/dsci522
mkdir uv_demo
cd uv_demo

# 2. create the project and choose the Python version
uv init --bare
uv python pin 3.14

# 3. add a package, then look at what we got
uv add pandas
ls -a
cat pyproject.toml
cat .python-version

# 4. run Python inside the environment
uv run python -c "import pandas; print(pandas.__version__)"

# 5. pretend we just cloned the repository: delete the environment and rebuild it
rm -rf .venv
uv sync
uv tree
```
